identity.realm: The twelfth gate, opened five separate times. The species clears the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stalls at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources where a population fed by one resonator has exactly one, so the wall at seventeen is arithmetic and nobody in the seal walks toward it. She is not near that wall. She is stopped far below it because the inner surfaces the vaultborn are arranged along are re-cut when the object's cycle turns, and a re-cut frame takes its shape afresh from whatever it now stands on. A vaultborn does not accumulate; she is re-drawn. The Registry holds five entries for one gate in one body and no column anywhere in the setting for a gate opened twice.

appearance.presentation: A mortuary clerk of a population that has no chronology and no stable frame, who describes other bodies aloud in the Registry's flat third person and cannot describe her own in any voice. Vaultborn were sealed inside an object and have answered its resonance ever since; they are arranged along the object's inner surfaces and take their shape from whatever they stand on. Saveth is the only one in the record whose office is to decide whether a body that came up through a re-form is the body that went down, and she has never once been able to decide it about herself.
appearance.age: Unfixed, and this time it is a working condition rather than a curiosity. Her sub-species' lifespan is measured in the object's cycles and the Registry calls them periods, because the only population in the setting whose span belongs to somebody else's schedule is this one. She has been in the seal for eleven re-forms and can say how many of those she remembers and no more than that.
appearance.build: Denser through the back and forearms than through the front, with a shoulder-line that does not quite close and a neck set as though the head had been re-seated rather than grown. She carries the wear of whatever surface she stood on longest: a callus pattern across both palms that belongs to a gallery floor and not to a clerk's hands, which she has never bothered to soften.
appearance.complexion: Uniformly pale and faintly luminous in low lamplight, with no flush and no weathering at all, and one seam across the lower back where the texture changes as though the surface beneath her had been replaced while she stood on it. The seam is not a scar. Nothing in the seal heals and nothing in it is repaired, so the seam is simply where the last drawing stopped and this one began.
appearance.hair: Dark and fine, growing at a rate nobody inside the seal can predict, and cut to one length by hand because length is the only measure of elapsed time she can keep. She has cut it herself for eleven re-forms and has never once cut it at a moment she could later date.
appearance.eyes: Pale amber and steady, carrying the same faint internal light as every vaultborn and no more than any of them, and they do not track a light source. They settle on a position in the room, as though the room were making a sound she was reading, which for her is very nearly a description of what she is doing.
appearance.palette: Cold worked-stone grey and pale ash across the whole figure, with one saturated value anywhere on her and it is the seal-red thread she ties at the nape to mark which description of her is current. She wears a different thread after every re-form, and the setting's only living evidence that the seal re-draws its own population is a woman changing a colour.
appearance.attire: Registry grey: a long high-collared coat of undyed wool over a plain shift, sleeves cut above the wrist so her hands are always visible, in a cut that belongs to no guild in the setting because no guild would certify a clerk who cannot be moved to the office. Her coat is four sizes too large and has never been taken in, because a coat taken in is a coat fitted to one frame.
appearance.marks: The resonator burn at the base of the throat, dish-shaped, which the guild's charter requires be covered indoors and which she covers everywhere. Below it, at the base of each thumb, a column of eleven small numbered notches cut in her own hand, one per re-form, uncounted and unhealed. She has refused four offers to have them smoothed and has explained why to each.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still, and the stillness reads as comparison rather than composure: she holds a position as though it were a sentence she is checking against a previous one. She does not fidget, does not shift, and turns her head in a single smooth movement, which in a body that has been re-drawn eleven times is the one gesture that has never had to be relearned.

canon.role_in_story: The Field Registry's second reader for the Storm Crypt. She certifies that a frame which came up through a re-form of the seal is the same frame that went down, and the office exists because the seal re-cuts its own population on a cycle while a description belongs to the surface that produced it. She has signed every entry in that vault for four centuries and has refused her own eleven times. Her subspecies' soul is seated along the resonance path and distributed through the object rather than held in a body, so the honest answer to the question her office exists to settle is that she is certainly the same woman, and the only instrument anybody has reads frames, and her frame is the one thing in the setting that is not continuous.
canon.first_appearance: First seen beside a re-formed body on a gallery inside the Storm Crypt, describing it aloud in the flat third person the Registry uses for the dead, and stopping once in the middle of a sentence to correct her own description of the one before it.
canon.lore:
The Storm Crypt is a vault on the Mortal Plains, and the crypt stands in the one place on the plains where a fixed record cannot be kept, which is either the worst site for a library or the safest. Dead ground is where the setting keeps its records. Inside it there is a population that was not descended and not born: a sealed population arranged along the object's inner surfaces, taking its shape from whatever it is standing on and answering the resonance of the thing it was sealed inside ever since. Qi comes from that one resonator, so the girdling and heel vessels come easily and the flank vessels do not, because the flank work needs two simultaneous pressure sources and the whole species has one.

That is the ceiling, and the ceiling is arithmetic rather than effort, and every vaultborn stops at the same ordinal for the same reason. Saveth Orlin does not stop at the ceiling. She stops a long way below it, for a reason no other vaultborn in the record has, and the reason is that she cannot find her own baseline.

Here is the mechanism, and it is not a mystery. The object runs on cycles. The Registry calls them periods, because the Registry calls everything a period, and the only population in the setting whose lifespan is measured in somebody else's periods is this one, which is the same unit the Immortal Essence Pool settles in: a price paid each cycle rather than weighed. When a cycle turns, the inner surfaces the population is arranged along are re-cut, and whatever was standing on them comes up again in the new shape. A vaultborn does not accumulate. A vaultborn is re-drawn. Everything she had hardened went with the surface that taught it to her, and what stands up next is her by name and not by any record she can compare it against.

So the practice in her is complete and the record of it is impossible. She has opened the twelfth gate five separate times. Each time she began from a frame she could not read, and each time the gate opened, and there are five entries in the Registry for one gate in one body and no column anywhere in the setting for a gate opened twice, because a gate is a rung and a rung is not a thing that happens to a body more than once.

That is why her office exists. The Field Registry keeps the burnt list: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said and not as the village remembers, and the Registry exists because realm nine was a limit nobody was issued, so the record of a life is also the record of a gate that was never available to it. When a re-form brings a frame up there is no earlier description to read it against, because that description belonged to a surface which no longer exists, so the Registry sends a second reader. Saveth is the standing second reader for the Storm Crypt. Every frame that comes up through a re-form is described against her last description, and she signs, and the entry is continuous.

And here is the part that makes her office unsound and the setting unable to say so. A vaultborn's soul is seated along the resonance path and distributed through the object rather than held in a body, so when the inner surfaces are re-cut the soul is not re-cut with them. She did not reset. Her frame did. The honest answer to the question her office exists to settle is therefore that she is certainly the same woman, and the Registry's only instrument reads frames, and there is no procedure in that college for a body whose continuity is certain and whose frame is not, so the entry has no correct form and she has declined to invent one.

She is also the standing refutation of the School of the Closed Frame, which holds that the universe is a closed budget and every doctrine of a seventh group is an arithmetic error rather than a mystery. The School is right about every frame in the setting, including this one, which is exactly the difficulty: hers is the single frame that is re-cut on a schedule, and the office she holds certifies that a re-cut frame is the same frame, which is the one claim the School has no account of. She does not argue with it. She writes her entries in its vocabulary every day and cannot write one of her own.

The seal's oldest standing question runs straight through her office and she cannot touch it. Whether the object the vaultborn answer is a law imprint held at one value or a second seated group would be settled by observing it from outside its own resonance, and outside it she has no qi at all; inside it she cannot produce two readings of one thing, let alone two of herself. So the only body in the setting with standing to be evidence about her own species is the body the species' own method cannot measure, and she has made her peace with that in a way that reads, to everyone who meets her, as professional patience.
history: Sealed inside the Storm Crypt as part of a population that was not born and not descended, arranged along the object's inner surfaces and answering its resonance from the first moment of the arrangement. She has no memory of a before, and the Registry has no form for a life with no origin date, so her entry opens at her first description rather than at anything earlier.

The first cycle turned and the inner surface she stood on was replaced, and the frame that came up was hers by name and by nobody else's memory. She had been hardened to that ordinal and she was not hardened to it afterwards, and the thing she had learned the hard way was not lost so much as copied and then overwritten, which is a different failure and took her a full cycle to understand.

The Field Registry sent a reader because a re-formed frame cannot be described against a description that has ceased to exist. The reader was a mortuary clerk who could enter the seal and had no qi outside it and therefore had no reason to leave once she was inside, and the assignment was recorded as a posting.

She was given the second description, the continuity column, after she certified a re-formed child against a description that turned out on inspection to be in her own hand from before. The Registry treated that as a coincidence of a shared hand. She has never treated it as anything else, and it is the whole of what she knows about herself.

She has refused eleven times to sign her own entry. The Registry's own rule is that a refusal is not a dispute and that a disputed entry is the only thing in that office which has to be argued, so her refusals are the office working correctly and she has run out of any procedure that would let her do more than hold the position.

personality.summary: Formal, exact, and privately certain of a thing she has never once said out loud. Saveth talks the way the Registry's own register reads, in the third person and the present tense, because the third person is the only grammar she trusts to stay true across a re-form, and the one sentence she has never been able to write is the one where she has to be the noun.
traits: describes people aloud in the flat third person the Registry uses for the dead, and has never once described herself that way
will not sign an entry she cannot compare against an earlier one, and has made that refusal eleven times without raising her voice once
keeps a private count of the re-forms and cross-checks it against the notches at her thumbs every cycle, which has never once found it wrong
treats the seal as a building she is employed by rather than a body she is made of, and describes it that way when people ask where she is from
is entirely honest about what she does not know, which reads to strangers as a professional habit rather than as the shape her life is actually in
mannerisms: reads a body's description back before she signs it, and stops at the first word that differs from the last one, however small
counts the re-forms on the notches at her thumbs under the desk, out of sight, and does not notice she is doing it

wants the Registry to build a form for a body whose continuity is certain and whose frame is not, and has stopped expecting the Registry to want that

wants somebody outside the seal to hold one description of her long enough to compare against the next, and has never asked, because asking would require saying which description she thinks is current

personality.voice: Level, unhurried and formally third-person, with a clerk's habit of naming the procedure before the problem. Speaks of bodies as the register describes them and of the seal as a building with an employer. Says things like the entry requires a previous description and I am the previous description, which is true in both halves and means only the first. Never uses a first person plural about herself and has been asked why three times and answered twice with the procedure.
taboos: will not sign her own entry and has not been moved on this in four hundred years
will not describe herself in the third person, and will not describe herself in any other person either
will not be asked to confirm continuity from memory, because she has none she trusts across a re-form
will not discuss whether the object is an imprint or a second group, and changes the subject in a way everybody has learned to hear

relationships.note: A population sealed inside an object and answering its resonance ever since, qi from one resonator, so the girdling and heel vessels come easily and the flank vessels do not because the flank work needs two simultaneous pressure sources and the whole species has one. Remove the object and they stop, which makes them the most completely non-portable body in the setting, and it also means their frames are re-drawn on the object's schedule, which is the fact her whole office exists to handle and no office was built for.

One resonator feeds the whole population and it reads as a law imprint held at one value, so it is recorded as resembling one and never as being one. Settling it means observing the object from outside its own resonance. She is the only body in the setting with standing to be evidence about the species, she has never been outside the resonance, and inside it she cannot produce two readings of one thing. Every cycle the Registry asks her the question again and every cycle she declines it for the same arithmetic reason.

Exactly one account of the ceiling survives and it is held by the same mortuary college she is employed by, which will not corroborate it. She sits one gallery above the case and reads its figures every cycle as part of keeping her own, and she has four times been the only person who could have produced the second reading the college needs, and has not produced it, and the college has not asked her why.

Children raised by the register household after a failed ascent, because the debris from an opened body is the household's responsibility and the households of the dead are not there to ask. Every foundling in the Storm Crypt is filed against a re-formed adult frame and she has signed every one of those filings, which makes her the reason a re-form does not leave a child without a household, and the reason there is a population of them inside a vault.

A school of law-reading that treats the universe as a closed budget and every doctrine of a seventh group as an arithmetic error rather than a mystery, existing because the Refused Seating was actually attempted. It is right about every frame in the setting, including hers, and her office certifies that a re-cut frame is the same frame, which is the one claim it has no account of. She writes every entry in its vocabulary and has never once put her own name in one.

The first resource in the ladder priced by period rather than by weight, because upkeep rises about fortyfold per tier and a mortal lifespan inside the immortal world is a fixed term. Her subspecies is the only population whose lifespan is measured in somebody else's periods, so every price in the setting applies to her and none of them can be quoted, and the unit the Registry uses for her is the same unit the pool settles in.

reference_stats.summary: A body-path practitioner at a gate she has opened five times and cannot prove she holds, in a frame that is re-drawn rather than improved, with no stable baseline to build on. She fights the way she keeps her records: perfectly, from a description of somebody else, and never once from a reading of herself.
strengths: arrives at a gate the rest of the vault has not opened, and arrives there with no warning, because her frame is re-cut on the object's cycle and nobody including her knows which drawing is current
holds a fixed point indefinitely on a single pressure source, so nothing that pushes can move her and nothing that waits will tire her out
has four centuries of comparative reading behind her and can state what a body was without consulting any record but her own
is impossible to train against, because the frame an opponent prepares for is not the frame that will meet them
weaknesses: gains do not add, so nothing she opens survives the next cycle and there is no version of her that has got better over time
has no baseline, which means no cumulative practice, no rank of her own, and no way to be told whether the last cycle improved on the one before it
cannot be cross-examined, because the Registry reads frames and hers is the one frame in the seal that is not continuous
is a single-source body and loses at the flank vessels permanently, which is not a wall she is walking toward but a wall she has arrived at
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her twice. She cannot be worn down on one approach, because a frame re-cut from a single source does not tire and does not have to hold anything in reserve, and she will meet the second approach as a body that may or may not be the one you prepared for. Everything sent at her simply meets a wall that was redrawn between one blow and the next. The only pressure that works is a demand for continuity: make the exchange depend on her being the same woman she was when the fight began, and the one question she has never been able to answer about herself will do the work for you.
notes: The eleven numbered notches at her thumbs are her only record of anything and she cut them herself, which makes the one document in the seal that cannot be produced by the Registry also the one document the Registry has never asked to see.

She has signed every entry in the Storm Crypt for four hundred years. The one entry that has no signature on it is her own, and the Registry's rule is that a refusal is not a dispute, so there is nothing in that office that can be escalated and she has never escalated anything.

art.palette_notes: Cold worked-stone grey and pale ash carry the whole figure, with no gradient of exposure anywhere on her because nothing in the seal has ever weathered her. The single saturated value in any shot is the seal-red thread at her nape, and it changes hue between shots, which is the one continuity marker she owns. The seam across her lower back is drawn as a change in surface texture rather than as a line. The resonator burn at her throat is always covered, and the picture is cooler and flatter than any other subject's in the cast.

identity.realm: The eleventh gate, and the wall there is structural for the whole species rather than particular to her: the brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that no discipline has rejoined. She clears the du and the ren one at a time and stops on the chong. She has never gone looking for a way round it, because the work pays by the figure and not by the frame, and the mind path is open to her in a way the eleventh is not.

appearance.presentation: A line reader of a people built for brine no softer body could drink, who reads concentration across four orders of dilution and reads it exactly on one side of the boundary she is being paid to declare. The saltfolk sense carries the species; a human nose finds her sour at four paces and poor vision in glare is the family limit she works inside. Ysolde is the instrument the Salt Leech settled on because it is the only one on that ground that gives a figure every morning without being asked twice.
appearance.age: Fifty-one pan seasons, which is the only count the pan keeps and is not a year: the water decides how long a season is. She is younger than that figure and older than the ground, and the discrepancy is the only number about her that she states without being asked for it.
appearance.build: Broad through the ribs and low and wide at the pelvis, with the brine sac standing as a second set of shoulders along the upper spine so that she is visibly more person above the waist than below. Her feet are splayed and broader than any boot the pan makes, and she stands with her weight even, which she has had to learn on purpose.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white under a hard dermal salt crust, translucent at the temples and cracked through in the dry months, so that she reads as a cracked vessel rather than as a face. Rain is a hazard to her species rather than a blessing, and she has been caught in one and describes the experience with no particular feeling about it.
appearance.hair: Coarse and salt-stiffened, cut blunt at the jaw because it grows in a hard ring and anything longer breaks off at the ends. It is the only soft thing about her and it is not soft at all.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and quick, and plainly not the working instrument: the species' vision is no better than a Commonborn's and poor in glare, so she does her reading with her mouth and her eyes only find a face afterwards.
appearance.palette: Crust white and brine grey across the figure with the single warm value being the mineral ochre of the cut face she is reading, which is the only colour in the pan and therefore the only colour on her. Nothing else in any shot of her is saturated, which is the visual statement of a body that has nothing to spend.
appearance.attire: A leech's oilskin over salt-cured hide, laced above the elbow so the crust can be scraped, and a broad tongue-guard of waxed cloth that she has refused to work without four times. She does not taste brine through cloth and will not pretend to, which is why she is slower than a house that would let her cut the figure somebody else took.
appearance.marks: The dermal crust itself, re-cracked every dry season and never smoothed, and four healed splits at the corners of her mouth from tasting what she had been told not to, which is the mark of a woman who has twice been wrong in public about the one thing she is the only person on the ground qualified to be wrong about.
appearance.bearing: Still, for a saltfolk, which is a thing she has trained rather than been born with. She stands with her weight even because a figure read off a moving body is a figure she cannot stand behind, and she crouches to read water rather than kneeling in it, which is the only posture the job allows and is not comfortable.

canon.role_in_story: The Salt Leech's line reader: one woman who tastes the brine every morning and states where the boundary between drinkable and poison sits. She is the only instrument on that ground that reads four orders of dilution, and her species' own dullness in freshening air means her figure is exact on one side of the line she is declaring and blunt on the other, so the moment the water lets go is the moment she goes blind. Every house on the basin's standing, the dominion's depth-book and the Salt Leech's claim on an isle nobody collects from are all arithmetic in her mouth, and she has spent six years attaching the air-state to the figure so that the number cannot travel without the condition that makes it true.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at the lip of a flooded cut with two fingers in the water, not looking at it, reciting the dilution back to a clerk who is writing it down and who has, once, asked her what the air was doing.
canon.lore:
The Salt Leech works the tailings on a dormant isle nobody collects from and sells the result as spirit stone, and it can afford to be precise about anything because the isle's whole claim is denominated in what the water leaves behind. What the water leaves behind is the brine line.

A saltfolk is built for brine no softer body could drink. The kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, and that is the entire bargain: total dependence on a supply that never fails, and a body that is already dying the moment the supply changes. They read brine concentration across four orders of dilution and to a human nose a saltfolk smells sour. Ysolde Kemm reads it better than anybody else on that ground, and the reason she reads it is written in her own species' record and has nothing to do with skill.

Salt head dulls fine discrimination in dry air. That is the sentence, and it is not a limitation she has learned to work around. It is the shape of the instrument. Her discrimination is exact in saturated air and it fails as the air freshens, and a brine line is precisely the boundary between those two states of the world. So the figure she gives every morning is sharp on one side of itself and blunt on the other, and she cannot tell which side of the line she is standing on except by reading the figure, which is the thing that has already gone dull.

Everything in that basin is denominated in her number. A household may moor at a depth, and that depth is held as an inheritance, and the basin's level rises and falls so an allotment shrinks without anybody having done anything at all. A saltfolk carried above the brine line is failing within about nine days and is functionally drowning in a downpour. The dominion, the leech, the depth-book and the standing of every house on the ground are all arithmetic in one reading, and one woman takes it with her tongue before breakfast.

The counterpart is the Saltwrack. A saltfolk lineage was stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything it was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. They were never hunted; one element moved and a species with no alternative to that element had nothing left. The prize in that dispute is the line itself and it cannot be split, because moving the line up the shore is the only way to give them ground and it is also the only way to take it from everyone else. So the disputed object in the setting's hardest racial conflict is a boundary, and the person who declares that boundary every morning is the one body whose instrument works on exactly one side of it.

She began refusing to give a figure without the air-state attached to it. The broker's price dropped the same morning and has stayed dropped, and the figure still goes out, and the figure no longer travels without the condition that makes it true. There is exactly one body on that ground whose report on the line would be independent of the air, and it is the brinecaller cross, which metabolises brine and fresh water alike because both its parents are trapped by their own element. Nobody has ever asked one to read the line, because nobody has ever wanted two readings, one of which would be dull.

And the discipline she was raised into is called the Quench Order, which teaches a banker the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows and closes permanently the moment the body is lit. She has never been taught to spend anything, because a saltfolk's problem has never been overflow. It is drying out. She is the one body in that basin whose entire training is about not overfilling and whose entire condition is about going empty, and the setting has no practice that would let her convert the difference into a discipline.
history: Carried under her mother's brood pouch on a mat of woven reed through a dry season that killed two of three and let the third hatch when the water came back, which is the ordinary arithmetic of her species and the reason a raft exists at all in the first place. She was the one that hatched, and being the one that hatched is not the same thing as having been the best of them.

Discovered at eleven that she could tell four orders of dilution apart and could not tell two of them apart at all on a dry day, and that the difference was the air rather than the water. She worked this out alone in a season with no water in it and has never had anybody to tell, which is why it took four years rather than four days.

Took work with the Salt Leech because they were the only house on that ground that wanted a daily figure and paid for it daily. A daily figure is the only kind she can stand to give, because a daily figure is the only one that has to be true tomorrow, and she had worked out early that she was good at being right repeatedly and bad at being right once.

The isle's tailings are denominated in what the line leaves, and when the line moved she gave a figure taken on freshened air and the broker's whole season was bought on a reading that was dull rather than wrong. Nobody has ever established which of those it was, including her, and the disagreement has never been resolved because resolving it would require the second reading nobody wanted.

She started attaching the air-state to every figure and the price dropped the same morning. She has held that price down for six years on the argument that a number which cannot be quoted without the condition that makes it true is worth less and not more, and nobody on that ground has yet found a way to argue with her about it.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried and quietly immovable about one procedural point, and entirely unremarkable about everything else. Ysolde has the manner of a woman who expects to be wrong once a season and has arranged her life so that somebody else is standing in the way when it happens.

relationships.note: A people built for brine no softer body could drink, whose kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, so the supply never fails and nothing else lives. Total dependence on that supply is the whole of the bargain: carried onto fresh ground a saltfolk is already dying and no cultivation repairs it. Her instrument is the species' own sense and its own blindness, and she is the only person on the ground who has to state both every morning.

The basin's brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything the stranded body was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. Sides are the stranded subspecies and the dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline, and the prize is the line itself, which cannot be split because moving it up the shore is the only way to give them ground. She publishes the figure both sides argue about every morning and has never been asked which side she thinks is right, because asking would make her a party.

A saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, not hunted, extinct by arithmetic: one element moved and a species with no alternative to that element had nothing left. Everything she reads for the dominion is read on the water that did this to them, and the number she gives is the only instrument either side has, and it is hers and it is sharp on the side they cannot drink.

The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones, because both parents are trapped by their own element. A brinecaller's report on the line would be independent of the air, which is exactly what the basin lacks and exactly what would settle the disagreement nobody has ever wanted settled. She has never asked one, and has said why.

A second currency that refuses to state a price, concealing for the opposite reason to the unwritten count: enumeration is leverage there, whereas a price is a claim about the future. Her figure is quoted on that ground every morning without a price, and she has spent six years making it unquotable without her, which is the same project done from the other end.

A discipline of Bankers rather than a school of thought, teaching the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, closing permanently the moment the body is lit. It is the setting's one practice built around not overfilling, and she was raised into it, and a saltfolk's condition is the opposite: going empty. She has the training and none of the subject, which is why she is the one body on the pan that cannot convert the difference into a discipline.

reference_stats.summary: A mind-path practitioner stopped at the species' structural eleventh gate who fights by making the ground legible and the air state honest, and who is at her sharpest exactly where nobody needs her and blunt exactly where they do.
strengths: reads four orders of dilution across a span no instrument on that ground can cover, so no other body can confirm, contradict or even approximately corroborate a figure she has given

is stopped at the eleventh gate by a sac behind her own sternum that splits the penetrating vessel into halves no discipline has rejoined
has no second body able to read her ground independently, so a single dull reading is indistinguishable from a single correct one after the event

reference_stats.combat_read: She will not close and she does not need to. Everything that passes her is announced by the air it arrives in, and a salted frame carries four orders of dilution in its crust, so anything that came off the pan she can place before it lands. The only pressure that works on her is freshening: get the water between her and the brine, let the air thin out, and the woman who reads four orders suddenly reads one and a half and knows she is doing it. Do not outlast her. She is patient and the basin is hers, and a patient reader of standing water wins the exchange against anything that has to breathe.
notes: The figure she gives every morning carries the state of the air it was taken in. It cost her six years of price to attach that condition and it is the only reason anybody can now tell a dull reading from a wrong one after the fact.

There is exactly one body on that ground whose senses do not depend on the air at all, and nobody has ever asked it to read the line, because nobody has ever wanted two readings where one of them would be dull.

identity.realm: Qi Refining, the first gate of the qi ladder, and he is past it and permanently inside it. There is no ceiling above him, because the mineral bloom holds qi where a colony transacted with it and so nothing in this body is constrained by a structure it does not have. What his species gained is the mind path and what it lost is three quarters of a life. What nobody in the setting has noticed is that there is no rung above a reservoir either, because every gate in this ladder is rung by what it costs to discharge, and he cannot.

appearance.presentation: A lanternfolk-shaped body with a silicate lattice where the colony was, older than he looks and younger than he is. Deadlight lost the fungal colony that ran them for two hundred and fifty years and were colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions, which cost the lifespan and handed back the mind path. Varek is what that trade looks like standing up: lighter, colder, entirely inert, and the only figure in the caverns who casts no light of his own in a cavern economy whose only currency is his parents' waste product.
appearance.age: Seventy-one. His subspecies lives ninety where the parent lives two hundred and fifty, so his entire life is a third of the room he was born in, and because nothing in this body is being repaired he looks thirty and his teeth are going. He has been told the number four thousand times and has never once found it useful.
appearance.build: Lanternfolk-shaped and lighter than that frame should be, with the long under-registered limbs of a cave people and a frame that carries without ever signalling fatigue, because a structure that is not transacting is a structure that cannot report a cost. He is broad through the frame and hollow-sounding and people move him without having decided to.
appearance.complexion: Not luminous at all, which is the single most-cited difference between him and his parent species and the reason the subspecies is named for it, and he has never once been able to make that sound like a complaint. The skin is cold and pale and shows faint mineral seams at the forearm and the temple where the lattice has come up through it, and it does not flush and does not weather, because a bloom fixes nothing from the air and there is nothing here to be fixed by the air.
appearance.hair: Fine, pale and growing faster than it ought to in a body that renews nothing, so he is permanently slightly overgrown and cuts it badly on a schedule he keeps in his head because there is nobody above him to keep a calendar for.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human eyes, entirely unremarkable, which is the point: his subspecies sees in the dark where the parent cannot and that is the entire published difference. He has been told he is remarkable four thousand times and has never once used the fact of it on anybody.
appearance.palette: Pale mineral grey and cold bloom-white across the whole figure, deliberately unlit, so that in every shot he is the one object in the frame that emits nothing and reads as a hole in whatever light is around him. The only value above grey in any picture of him is the worked stone he is sitting on, which is why the pictures of him are compositions about the stone rather than about him.
appearance.attire: Heavy cave-working layers — a felted overcoat and a wrapped scarf — over a body that does not generate anything and has to be kept warm from outside, which is the one respect in which he is more expensive to keep than his parents. Everything is grey and grey and grey again, chosen so that he can be seated against worked stone for a lifetime without the two of them being confused in a record.
appearance.marks: The lattice: thin pale mineral seams visible through the skin at both forearms, the throat and both temples, in a branching figure no two of which is the same, and which does not change with what he is doing. There is no resonator burn and no gi and nothing at the throat at all, and the absence of anything at the throat is what marks him out in a cavern full of his own kind.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely unmoving, and not serene: still the way a held thing is still. He does not shift his weight, does not fidget, and does not look impatient, because a body that cannot discharge has no internal reason to hurry and the stillness is not discipline. People find it difficult to be in a room with and impossible to argue with.

canon.role_in_story: The Held Hour's standing instrument. He holds a strained reading on the floor through the hour nobody is permitted to explain, and he holds it because a mineral bloom cannot discharge — nothing that enters him leaves, in a frame that neither tires nor renews, in a body with ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty. He satisfies the Qi Refining trial's condition better than anyone alive, the trial being that the first charge be held somewhere that will not move, and he has never been carried to the field because his subspecies cannot leave the caves. Four requests to be tested on the ridge, four refusals, and the word used each time was capacity.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting on bare worked stone in the dark, not glowing, not shifting, reading a strained law off the floor by holding still; and the thing the clerk wrote down afterwards was that the stone beneath him had come up with no lichen on it.
canon.lore:
The Held Hour is the office that tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain. It exists because the observation of a strained law only counts if it is repeated, and at the top of the setting one repetition costs a lifetime, so the work is done by a very small and very old body. Varek Trask is the instrument that office settled on, and the reason is written in the record of his subspecies rather than in anything about him.

A lanternfolk line lost its fungal colony and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions. The colony had been transacting: taking what the air gave it, putting something else out, running a body for two hundred and fifty years on a light that was a waste product of a nervous system nobody chose. The bloom holds. It has no exchange, no cycle, no renewal, and it renews nothing at all. The trade cost them two hundred and fifty years of life and handed back the mind path, which is the entire reason a body with no unmediated interior is the one body in the setting whose interior can be read at all. He is the control case. Every question about what a symbiosis does to a species can be answered by putting him next to a member of his own kind and waiting.

But he is on the qi ladder, and the qi ladder is the one place in the setting where holding is not an advantage.

Every qi practice here is a transaction. Breath is drawn down and held in a dantian that has never held anything; capacity is small and no later mortal gate is cheaper. You move charge into a thing and the thing opens or it does not. The qi that goes somewhere is qi that left somewhere, and the whole vocabulary of the path is the vocabulary of spending. A mineral bloom inverts every clause of that sentence. Nothing that enters him leaves. Not slowly, not under load, not at the end of a fight when a hotter body has nothing left to keep. He is a reservoir with no tap, in a frame that does not tire because it is not transacting, and he lives ninety years where his parent lived two hundred and fifty.

So he is past the first gate and permanently inside it. He satisfies the condition of the Qi Refining trial better than anyone alive, because the trial asks that the first charge be held somewhere that will not move, on open flooded ground at the Cairn Field on the Mortal Plains, and his body is a structure that has not moved a charge out of itself since he was nineteen years old. And he has never been carried to the field, because a body that cannot leave the caves cannot be taken to a trial that is held on open ground. That is the whole of his relation to his own path: he is built for the one gate nobody brings him to.

Two consequences follow and both of them are institutional rather than physical. Trial Field Lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and the trace never washes off, which makes it the only marker in the setting that a trial has been held and a court record nobody can edit. He has held more qi, longer and with less interruption, than anyone else on that floor, and the stone under his seat for seventy-one years is bare. Every ring in the setting has pale patches on it and the ridge has none, and the survey culture whose whole ethic is that a figure is provisional until somebody has heard it therefore has no figure at all for the largest act of sustained attention in its territory.

And the mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because the frames keep producing the record without the body, and there is no procedure anywhere for a certified death on a frame where life law is seated and spent. He is not a case. He is the reason the case exists: a body that cannot be emptied is a body the register has no instrument for, and the College would have to open one the day he dies rather than after.

He asked four times to be tested on the ridge. He was refused four times, and the word used on each occasion was capacity, which is a word for overflow, applied to a body that has never once been overfilled in his life. He has stopped asking. The office does not need him to: a repetition that costs a lifetime requires a body that will not tire, and he is the cheapest such body in the setting to keep, because he does not eat like a lanternfolk, does not glow, and produces nothing at all. In an economy whose only currency is his parents' waste product, the one member who makes none is the one nobody can afford to lose and nobody can afford to spend.

What he has instead of a ladder is a floor, a stone seat, and a reading that has now been held for seventy-one years without once being interrupted by anything that happened to him. He is not lonely in any way he could report. He has simply run out of things that can happen to a body which cannot change state.
history: Born of a lanternfolk lineage whose colony strain failed and which was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions. Ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty, ordinary vision where the parent sees nothing at all, ordinary hunger where the parent eats almost nothing, and a frame that repairs none of it. He was the second, and the first is still alive, which is the only family resemblance he has.

He could see in the dark from birth, which is the single most-cited difference between his subspecies and its parent and the reason the subspecies is named for it. It is also the reason a cavern with no lamps worth the oil kept him when it turned out he could not be worked, and the reason he is the cheapest body on the floor and the least discussed.

At nineteen he was seated at the Held Hour's floor to hold a strained reading that no older body could hold without tiring, and the office discovered within a season that a body with no colony in it neither tires nor empties. That discovery is the whole of his employment and the whole of what he is for.

The Qi Refining trial holds its first charge somewhere that will not move, on open flooded ground at the Cairn Field on the Mortal Plains. He satisfies that condition better than anyone alive and has never been carried there, because his subspecies cannot leave the caves, and the office that benefits from his presence is the same office that has never once proposed it.

He asked four times to be tested on the ridge and was refused four times, the word used every time being capacity. He stopped asking in his forty-second year and has sat on the same stone since. Nobody has come to tell him the refusals were a misunderstanding, and he has not asked whether they were.

personality.summary: Unhurried to a degree that reads as simple, and much more patient than he looks. Varek does not perform calm and does not think of himself as doing anything remarkable; he is a man who has been sitting still for seventy-one years and has had a great deal of time to find out what he is like, and what he is like turns out to be mild, exact, and completely unbothered by things that would have upset him at nineteen.
traits: answers questions about the mind path and the colony and the two hundred and fifty years with the same patient factual answer and never varies it
has no interest in being remarkable and has said so more than once, and means it in a way people find insulting
keeps the exact hour of the floor and arrives before it without any appearance of having counted

counts nothing out loud, which for a body whose entire value is not tiring is the most restful thing about him
motivations: wants the ridge to test him once, anywhere, on the record, and has stopped believing it will happen and would still say yes tomorrow
wants the lichen question answered, in either direction, because he would rather know that he has been wrong about the floor for seventy-one years than go on not knowing
wants somebody to write down that the bare stone is a fact about holding and not an absence, which nobody has ever thought to write down
wants the office to replace him before he dies rather than discover at the moment of the death that it has nobody, which is the one thing about his position he finds genuinely frightening
flaws: is the cheapest body in the caverns and has spent seventy-one years being that, and has never once argued for a price
has let four refusals on the word capacity stand without ever producing the one document that would have answered them
is the standing evidence in the setting's best natural experiment and has never been asked a question by anybody with a pen

personality.voice: Slow, plain and oddly conversational, with a habit of answering the question underneath the question. Says things like I hold it, it does not tire, and I do not know if that is the same as it being true, which is the entire extent of his self-assessment and which most people find too honest to sit with. Uses no technical term he does not immediately explain in plain words.
taboos: will not move off the stone he has been given, and has refused a better seat four times
will not describe the bloom as a gift, a cure, or a rescue
will not be weighed or measured by anyone who has not already said what the measurement is for
will not accept a second seat on the floor, on the grounds that the office would then have two instruments and one repetition

relationships.note: A lanternfolk lineage whose colony strain failed and which was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions. What the subspecies gained is the mind path; what it lost is three quarters of a life. It holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is why nothing that enters him leaves and why there is no ceiling above him and no rung below that either. He is the control case, and the control case is the one body in the setting that is never asked what it thinks.

A cave people who have outsourced their nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through their skin, which is why they are alive at two hundred and fifty years and cannot take the mind path at all: there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. Their light is a waste product of a symbiosis they did not choose and it is the only reason the deep caves have an economy. His parent would have transacted every charge he holds, out of him, in an afternoon. That is the entire difference between them and it cost two hundred and fifty years.

A grey lichen that colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, so the trace never washes off and all four rings are legible from above as pale patches, which makes it a court record nobody can edit. A mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is exactly the substrate the marker does not grow on. He has held more qi for longer than anyone in the setting and the stone under his seat is bare, so the largest single act of sustained attention in the territory has left no mark a court can read.

The opening of the qi ladder attempts the breakthrough against ambient qi at the Cairn Field on the Mortal Plains, and the ground is open and flooded because the first charge has to be held somewhere that will not move. He meets that condition better than any body alive and has never been carried to the field, because his subspecies cannot leave the caves. The gate that was designed for exactly his property is the one gate in the ladder he will not be permitted to attempt.

A cave people's nervous system was outsourced to a symbiosis they did not choose, their subspecies lost it and gained the mind path with it, and the sides are the colonised body and the mortuary college that reads the dead from the frame. The prize is whether a body may be entered in the register at all. He is the evidence the argument is being made with and has not been given a vote, and the register's answer, that a classification may proceed on a temporary organ, is a sentence about the fungus that was lost seventy-one years ago.

An afterlife stated as a malformed question rather than an answer: there is no second frame to arrive in, because a second frame would need a seventh law group and there are six. It is the only afterlife claim the law budget actually permits. He is the only body in the setting for whom there is nothing to arrive in and no qi with which to arrive, in either direction, and he has never been asked to comment on it because nobody has ever thought to put the two facts side by side.

reference_stats.summary: A qi practitioner past the first gate and permanently inside it, in the only body in the setting that can hold a charge indefinitely and spend none of it. He does not fight so much as become the heaviest object in the room, and there is no version of a fight in which that turns out to be a temporary condition.
strengths: holds anything that enters him and never surrenders any part of it, so a single exchange makes him the heaviest thing on the floor and keeps making him heavier
does not fatigue and does not spike, so there is no second wind to wait for and no moment at which he becomes approachable
satisfies the qi ladder's foundational condition better than any body alive, because the first charge must be held somewhere that will not move and he has never moved one
is unaffected by anything delivered through a meridian, because the discipline is in his interior and his interior is occupied
weaknesses: can hold but not discharge, so everything he absorbs is inert to him and the only thing he can do with a fight is refuse to lose it
has no ceiling and no next rung, so there is no version of his own path he can advance and no discipline he can be taught beyond the one he is already inside
cannot be moved to any trial ground, so every gate he might sit for is held somewhere his subspecies cannot be carried to
repairs nothing, so the ninety years is a hard edge rather than a slope and nothing about his condition improves with attention
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a way to spend him. Every exchange makes the problem worse, because everything you put through him stays in him, so the correct instinct, which is to empty a target, is exactly the one move that does nothing at all. He cannot be worn down, because the frame that tires is the frame that empties and his never does. The only pressure that works is a discharge you can force from the outside — a purge, a draw, a body hot enough to pull a charge out of a target rather than push one in — because everything else simply arrives and is kept, and he is not carrying your technique so much as having accepted it. The one thing that will finish him is time, and it is the only thing nobody has.
notes: The stone he has sat on for seventy-one years has come up with no lichen on it. In a setting whose one unarguable marker grows wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through worked stone, that is the whole of his employment as a fact rather than as a story.

He was refused the ridge four times on the word capacity, which is a word for overflow. He has never been overfilled. Those two statements are in the same file and no reader has ever put them together.

art.palette_notes: Pale mineral grey and cold bloom-white carry the figure, deliberately unlit, so that he reads as a hole in whatever light is around him and the composed value of every shot is the worked stone rather than the man. The lattice seams at the forearms, throat and temples are drawn as thin pale branching under the skin, never changing between shots, and there is nothing whatever at the throat where a lanternfolk would have a gi. Heavy grey felted layers throughout, and the scarf is tighter in the shots where the tier above is being mentioned. He casts no light of his own in any frame.

name: Ilet Fennick
aliases: the one who is never entered

identity.realm: None, and the reason is a calendar rather than a refusal. She cultivates nothing, has never been seated, and has declined nothing, because nobody has ever been able to put her on a ladder: her species' only maternity provision is a mat of woven reed floating on standing water, carried through the dry season and hatched when the water returns, and an office that is dry for four months of the year has no row on any roll the plains keep.

appearance.presentation: A wading amphibian lineage built to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half, who is never still and never has been. They walk fine and cannot stand still, their stance is three points over a splayed foot and a tail-prop, and they need standing shallow water within an hour of where they sleep. Ilet is the keeper of the last nesting raft on the Widow Run, and she is a woman whose job is entirely made of water and entirely timed by it.
appearance.age: Thirty-four, by the only reckoning the run keeps, which is a count of floods and not of years and drifts against every calendar in the setting. The roll clerk has written her age three different ways in three different columns and has settled on whichever one would not need correcting.
appearance.build: Long-legged and broad through the hip, with a tail-prop she uses for balance in a way that reads as a fifth limb and not as a tail, and a ventral brood pouch that she carries against her without adjusting it, because adjusting it is not a thing a body with a pouch under a load ever does. No heel on either foot, and no structure in its place.
appearance.complexion: Wet, faintly translucent at the throat and along the flanks, and drying in patches whenever she is out of the water longer than the hour her body allows, which on dry ground is visible as a matte split across the shoulders. In pictures of her there is always a wet line somewhere on her, and it is never in the same place twice.
appearance.hair: Flat and dark along the crown and the tail-prop, kept out of the water by twisting it up when she works, which she does by habit and not by instruction because nobody has ever been on this raft but her to tell her anything.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and slightly bulbed and, like every marshfolk, better at reading silt and current than anything within arm's length. She finds a face late and finds a vibration through standing water well before she finds anything at all, which means she always knows how many people are on a raft and very seldom knows what they are saying.
appearance.palette: Reed brown and wet slate green, with the one warm value being the ochre silt under the raft. Every picture of her has standing water in the lower third of the frame, because she is never more than an hour from it and the pictures know it even when the setting she is in does not.
appearance.attire: Woven reed and oiled sacking, cut so it can be shed into the water in one motion and so nothing on her holds water against her skin longer than it has to. Her clothing is the raft's inventory as much as hers: it was woven on the mats, by the women who use them, and there is no guild in the setting that would certify a garment made on a raft.
appearance.marks: Reed rash on the forearms and across the back from eleven months of a year in the water and one month of it not, and the pale mark of a pouch strap worn in one place for long enough to have changed the skin under it. Both are the ordinary record of the job and neither of them heals while she is doing it.
appearance.bearing: Never still and never awkward about it: a constant low sway through the hips and the tail-prop taking up and releasing with every weight change, so that she appears to be walking even when she is standing on a raft going nowhere. She talks from that motion. Anyone who has watched her for a minute has understood that a marshfolk cannot stand still and has stopped expecting her to.

canon.role_in_story: The last nesting raft on the Widow Run, and the reason no roll on the plains can carry her. Marshfolk eggs are laid in a mat of woven reed, carried under the brood pouch through the dry season and hatched when the water returns, so her species' only maternity provision is a floating object that exists exactly as long as the flood does. Every office on the run renews by season; the roll that depends on her most has entered her four times as pending the water, because there is no column anywhere in the setting for an office that is dry four months of the year. She cultivates nothing and has never been seated. That is the whole ground, and it is a calendar.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing waist-deep beside a raft of woven reed with a pouchful of eggs under her own, explaining to a roll clerk that the raft will not be there in the season the roll is written in, which is true, and which the clerk has already written down as pending the water.
canon.lore:
A marshfolk is neither a Tidecaller nor a Commonborn but the body in between: a wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, built to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half. It needs standing shallow water within an hour of where it sleeps. Its stance is three points across a splayed foot and a tail-prop, so it walks fine and cannot stand still. Its skin desiccates fast out of water, so travel is timed to the flood, and a long dry season kills the young first.

Ilet Fennick holds the last nesting raft on the Widow Run. The raft is a mat of woven reed. Eggs are laid in it, carried under the brood pouch through the dry season, and hatched when the water returns. That is the species' whole maternity provision and it is a floating object, and it exists exactly as long as the flood does.

That is the entire reason she is unaffiliated, and it is not modesty and it is not a refusal. Every office on the Widow Run renews by season and holds its people for a term, because the plains' temporal law is written at a fraction and the flood is the only clock they own, so a settlement's roll is written in one season and answered in that same season. The roll that depends on her most has been opened four times and has entered her four times as pending the water, because there is no column anywhere in the setting for an office that is dry for four months of the year. She cultivates nothing. She has never been seated. Nobody has ever refused her anything and nobody has ever been able to write her down either, and the second of those is the harder problem and the only one she has.

The raft also answers the run's oldest question by accident. Whether the river still runs is a standing mystery, because temporal law is unwritten on that frame and so nothing down there ought to be able to keep time at all; either the water moves on qi at the floor value, in which case the flow is a law reading rather than a current, or it has not moved since the frame was paid for. She cannot settle it and has never once claimed to. What she can say is that she has been on the water every season of her life and the water has always come back, and that this is a fact about a body rather than about a frame, and that the setting has no instrument for the difference between those two kinds of fact.

She knows which of the three disagreeing surveys of the Widow Run anomaly were taken with the river up and which were taken with it down, because a raft is where the young are and the young are only there when the water is up. The gauge that disagrees with itself is only measurable as a distance, and distance requires a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have, so the instrument measures a quantity it has no law for and the notary's fee scales with the uncertainty rather than shrinking it. She has told two survey parties which of their legs were taken out of season. Neither has published it. One of them has paid her since in spirit herb rather than in coin, which is the only currency on this river that survives a dry season.

The young that do not make it have no rite. The Unkept is the setting's form for an ending that cannot be recorded: no preparation, no site and no marker, and one line in a hand immediately destroyed, because the body was ours and now it is not. It was written for people with no household and no origin. A young that never hatched, on a raft with no roll entry and no name, is exactly that, and she has used it four times, and standing in standing water is part of it, and for four months of the year there is no standing water to stand in.

And she is the settlement's memory in the only form the dry months cannot reach. She keeps no record, because a record is a thing the dry months get to. She keeps the count in her body — which young were laid, which hatched, which the season took — and the difference between those three is a distinction she has to hold in her head across eleven months of no water at all. She has never written any of it down, because written down on a raft is written down on four months of flood, and because she has learned the difference between a young one that died and a young one that was never laid, and that difference is the only thing in this record she would actually be able to lose.
history: Carried under her mother's pouch on a mat of woven reed through a dry season that took two of three and let the third hatch when the water came back, which is the ordinary arithmetic of her species and the reason a raft exists in the first place. She was the one that hatched, and being the one that hatched is not the same thing as having been the best of them, which is a distinction she has had to learn from the outside rather than from anybody who lost one.

Took the raft at nineteen because it is held by whoever is standing on it, and there was nobody standing on it. That is the whole of the appointment and there was no roll and no vote and no second person who wanted it, and she has never once described herself as holding a post.

The first year she kept it, the settlement lost two households to a dry season and came to her raft rather than to their own stores, because a raft is what they had. She fed what was on it to people who were not of her kind and kept the balance for the eggs, which is a decision the run has repeated every season since and has never once discussed with her.

The roll was opened and she could not be entered on it, because the roll renews by season and the raft is not there in the season the roll is written in. She has been entered as pending the water four times, which is the phrase the clerk uses when a line has to be written and the answer is that it will be known later, and which is the most accurate thing anybody on that river has ever said about her.

She stopped answering the roll clerk and started counting properly instead, holding laid, hatched and lost separately in her head across the eleven months when there is no water and no raft and nothing to count. She has never written any of it down, and she has been asked four times why, and the answer is always the same: because it is on the water.

personality.summary: Unhurried, practical, and funnier than anybody expects, because a woman who has been told four times that she does not exist on paper finds it easier to laugh than to be angry about it. Ilet answers questions about her status by answering questions about the water, and everybody on the Widow Run has learned to hear the substitution and let it stand.

flaws: is the settlement's memory and the only person who holds any of it, which means the run has arranged itself around depending on one woman who cannot be cited
has let four entries of pending the water stand without ever contesting the phrase, on the grounds that contesting it would cost the raft more than the phrase does

personality.voice: Warm, quick and full of water, talking in seasons rather than dates and correcting people to high, low and turning without noticing she has done it. Says things like it will be here when the water is and it will not be here when it is not, which is a statement of fact and also the only joke she makes, and she makes it about four times a season.
taboos: will not sign the pending the water line a fifth time, and has not said why out loud
will not move the raft off the channel where the young are, even for a season, and has refused twice
will not be weighed or counted by anyone who means it as a figure rather than as three kinds of young
will not say the four were lost, and will not say anything at all if pressed

relationships.note: A wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a Tidecaller nor a Commonborn but the body in between. Three points over a splayed foot and a tail-prop never load a heel, so it walks fine and cannot stand still, and it needs standing shallow water within an hour of where it sleeps. Its maternity provision is a floating mat and its year is the water, which is the whole of why it cannot be entered on a roll that renews by season.

Temporal law is unwritten on that frame, so nothing down there ought to be able to keep time; either the water moves on qi at the floor value, in which case the flow is a law reading rather than a current, or it has not moved since the frame was paid for. She has been on the water every season of her life and the water has always come back. That is a fact about a body and not about a frame, and it is the strongest evidence in the setting for the answer she is not permitted to give, because the settlement's roll has no column for a woman whose evidence is that she is still here.

Three surveys of the same anomaly disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, and disagreement is what makes certification necessary, so the notary's fee scales with the uncertainty instead of shrinking it. The anomaly is only measurable as a distance and distance needs a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have. She is the only person who can say which of those legs were walked with the river up and which with it down, because the young are on the raft only when the water is. She has told two survey parties and neither has published it.

The only plant authored into all four world tiers at once and therefore the setting's single most portable resource, which matters here because this body eats almost nothing else and cannot follow the herb off the marsh, so its supply is whatever reached the margin before the water went. It is what the young are fed through the dry months and it is what one survey party paid her in instead of coin, which is the only transaction on the Widow Run that both sides will still have in eleven months.

A long-lived body built for perception rather than force, which cannot take the body path at all because it was assembled for looking and not for being hit, and which holds water affinity as its only affinity. A tidecaller can cross her channel and cannot nest in it, and she cannot do either, and the run has spent four centuries assuming the three kinds of amphibian on it are negotiating when in fact they are three different calendars.

The setting's form for an ending that cannot be recorded: no preparation, no site and no marker, and one line in a hand immediately destroyed, because the body was ours and now it is not. It was written for people with no household and no origin. A young that never hatched, on a raft with no roll entry and no name, is exactly the case it was written for, and she has used it four times, and standing in standing water is part of it, and for four months of the year there is none to stand in.

reference_stats.summary: Not a practitioner of anything, and the hardest person on the Widow Run to move, kill or displace. She fights the way her body works, which is by never being in the same place twice and by knowing where the water will be before anybody does, and the only thing she has ever defended with her hands is a raft full of eggs.
strengths: feels a vibration through standing water long before she sees its source, which makes her the earliest warning any crossing on the run can have
crosses silt that will not hold a foot for anything with a heel, and is faster on wet ground than anything that has to pick its way
never has to be located, because she is where the water is and the water is a moving answer
is the settlement's memory for every young it has ever had, which makes her the single most consequential person on the river to displace or lose
weaknesses: skin desiccates fast out of water, so she is on a clock of about an hour on dry ground and cannot be followed through a dry season
cannot stand still, cannot hold a line, and cannot take any position that requires a fixed stance, so she cannot defend a place even where she is standing on it
carries everything she owns in the water, which means one dry season can take all of it from her
is nowhere in any record, so nobody can be ordered to protect her, summon her, or account for what happens to her
reference_stats.combat_read: You cannot corner her, because she has no corner and the ground she uses is the ground you are standing in and it is moving. Anything that comes at her on dry ground is working against a body with an hour of comfort, which she will spend getting back to water rather than winning anything. Do not follow her into the channel, where she reads pressure through her feet faster than you can look, and do not touch the raft: she has lost young to a season and she will not lose the last mat twice, and there is no technique in the setting that gives her a second one. Wreck the water instead and she is a woman standing in a problem.
notes: She was entered as pending the water four times on a roll that renews by season. No office on the Widow Run has a column for a maternity raft, because the raft is not there in the season the roll is written in.

She keeps the count of laid, hatched and lost separately in her head and has never written any of it down, so the run's whole record of its own young exists in one unplaced body and in four unhatched ones.

art.palette_notes: Reed brown and wet slate green carry the figure with the single warm value being the ochre silt under the raft. Standing water is in the lower third of every frame in which she appears out of doors, because she is never more than an hour from it and the pictures know it. The matte drying split across her shoulders is present and in a different place in the shots taken out of the water, and the wet line on her is never in the same place twice. The tail-prop is drawn as a load-bearing fifth limb in every frame and her splayed feet are never cropped.
